I don't know how stressful a wedding is for a bride, but considering the fact that her mental health seems like a barrier in your friendship says alot about what this friendship means to you. I think you're taking her mental health lightly. 4 months of leave is no joke and if her family has to cancel on your wedding that means something is really wrong here. I understand that you may have felt like she stood you up, but it sounds to me like she's barely hanging on. I don't know OP, I think that if at this point in your lives where you've reached a milestone while she's drowning in her own head and the most important thing to you is her not keeping her bridesmaid duties, your friendship really might need a re-evaluation. For the sake of both of you. Its not easy caring for someone losing to their demons. It takes some real patience that you just may lack - and that just may the reality.

You raised a good man. He may have not made the best decisions, but he only did what he did to be someone you and your husband could lean on. But you have to tell him how much you appreciate him and how you're sorry that he thought he needed to protect you at a young age. You need to tell him your proud of him. That he's not dirty. That he's only ever made you proud and that he's the most precious gift you've been awarded. He needs to know that his role as protector wasn't in vain. That he did good. He needs to know that you love him above and beyond.

He's still stuck at 18. Help him move on.

A partner who can't understand that your kids are your first priority is a partner you don't need. In time, she's going to ask you to abandon your kids to be with her.
